blocks.en: Before you choose a pronoun, look at **what comes right after the verb**. Is there a preposition? Is it a person or a thing? Those two questions decide which pronoun you need. The next steps take each pronoun one by one, then mix them.

head: what follows the verb
function
pronoun
example
rows: Je vois Marie. → Je la vois.
Je parle à Marie. → Je lui parle.
Je pense à l'examen. → J'y pense.
J'ai besoin de mon vélo. → J'en ai besoin.
Je parle de Paul. → Je parle de lui.

blocks.en: Look at the verb **as French uses it**, not as English or Czech does. *Regarder quelque chose* has no preposition, although English says *look **at***. *Téléphoner à quelqu'un* has *à*, although English says *call someone*.

Without a preposition, person and thing are the same: *le, la, les*. After **à**, a person gives *lui / leur* and a thing or a place gives *y*. After **de**, a thing gives *en* and a person keeps *de* + a stressed pronoun (*de lui*).

items.en: I talk to Paul.
items.fr: Je [[lui]] parle.

items.en: I'm thinking about the holidays.
items.fr: J'[[y]] pense.

items.en: I'm talking about the film.
items.fr: J'[[en]] parle.

items.en: I'm talking about Paul.
items.fr: Je parle [[de lui]].
items.note: de + person keeps de and takes lui, elle, eux

item.fr: Je pense à mes vacances. → J'___ pense.

blocks.en: For a COD: *le* (masculine singular), *la* (feminine singular), *les* (plural). *Le* and *la* become **l'** before a vowel. For a COI: *lui* (one person, man **or** woman) and *leur* (several people). *Me, te, nous, vous* work for both, see step 9.

item.fr: Je téléphone à mes grands-parents. → Je ___ téléphone.

blocks.en: *Écouter, regarder, chercher, attendre* take **no** preposition in French: *Je l'écoute, je l'attends*. *Téléphoner à, répondre à, ressembler à, obéir à* **do** take *à*: *Je lui téléphone*.
blocks.title: Different from English

blocks.en: *Leur* (to them) never takes an **-s**. *Leurs* with an s is the possessive: *leurs parents* (their parents).

items.en: Are you watching the match? Yes, I'm watching it.

items.en: Do you eat fruit? Yes, I do.

items.fr: Tu parles de ta sœur ? Oui, je parle d'elle.
items.en: Are you talking about your sister? Yes, I'm talking about her.

articles.title: Step 2: le, la, les in simple tenses

blocks.en: *Le, la, les* replace a person or a thing that comes **right after the verb, with no preposition**. In a simple tense the pronoun goes **just before the conjugated verb**, never after it as in English.

head: replaced word
pronoun
example

Lucas → Je l'aime. / l'histoire → Je l'écoute.

blocks.en: The pronoun takes the gender of the **French** word: *la voiture → la*, *le vélo → le*, even if it is a thing.

*Attendre, chercher, écouter, regarder* take a COD in French: *Je l'attends* (I'm waiting for him), *Je la cherche* (I'm looking for her).

articles.title: Step 3: le, la, les with an infinitive

blocks.en: When a conjugated verb is followed by an **infinitive** (*vais voir, veux acheter, peux faire*), the pronoun belongs to the infinitive. So it goes **right before the infinitive**, not before the first verb.

rows.en: I'm going to see the film.

blocks.en: Everything where an infinitive follows: the futur proche (*aller* + infinitive), *vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, aimer, préférer* + infinitive, and verbs with *à* or *de* before the infinitive (*commencer à, oublier de, essayer de*). Also after *pour* and *sans*.

articles.title: Step 4: le, la, les in negatives and questions
articles.fr: le COD, la négation et la question

blocks.en: The pronoun and its verb stick together. In a negative, **ne goes before the pronoun** and *pas* after the verb: *Je ne le vois pas.* In a question nothing moves, except with inversion, where the pronoun still stays **before** the verb: *Le vois-tu ?*

*Ne* goes in front of the whole block *pronoun + verb*. *Ne* before a vowel becomes *n'*, but before a pronoun it is just *ne*: *Tu n'aimes pas ce film → Tu ne l'aimes pas.* The same goes for *jamais, plus, rien*: *Je ne le vois jamais.*

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: With two verbs *ne ... pas* goes around the **conjugated** verb and the pronoun stays before the infinitive.

rows.en: I'm not going to see him.

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun
item.fr: Je ne veux pas manger [la soupe].
a: Je ne veux pas la manger.

blocks.en: With rising intonation or *est-ce que* the word order stays the same: *Tu le vois ? Est-ce que tu le vois ?* With inversion the pronoun stays in front, the subject moves after the verb with a hyphen: *Le vois-tu ?* With two verbs the inversion is on the first verb: *Vas-tu le voir ?*

item.task_en: Ask the question with inversion

blocks.en: Do not split the pronoun from its verb: *Je ne le vois pas*, not *Je le ne vois pas* or *Je ne vois pas le*.

items.en: That girl, do you know her?

articles.title: Step 5: le, la, les in the passé composé
articles.fr: le COD au passé composé et l'accord

blocks.en: In the passé composé the pronoun goes **before the auxiliary** (*avoir* or *être*). And because the COD now stands **before** the participle, the participle **agrees** with it: *la → -e*, *les → -s* or *-es*.
*Ai, as, a, avons, avez, ont* all start with a vowel, so *le* and *la* are always **l'** here. Only the participle tells you which one it was.

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: Often you cannot hear it (*mangé, mangée*), but you can with participles that end in a consonant: *pris → prise*, *mis → mise*, *fait → faite*, *écrit → écrite*, *ouvert → ouverte*.

blocks.en: *Ne* goes before the pronoun, *pas* after the auxiliary: *Je ne l'ai pas vu.* Questions: *Tu l'as vu ? Est-ce que tu l'as vu ? L'as-tu vu ?*

blocks.en: No agreement when the COD comes **after** the verb: *J'ai vu Marie* (no -e) but *Je l'ai vue*.
Only a COD in front makes the participle agree. *Lui, leur, y* and *en* never do (steps 7, 10 and 11).

articles.title: Step 6: lui, leur in simple tenses and with an infinitive

blocks.en: *Lui* (one person) and *leur* (several people) replace **à + a person**. They go in **the same places** as *le, la, les*: before the conjugated verb, or before the infinitive.
Verbs of giving and communicating usually take *à* + person: you give something **to** someone, you say something **to** someone.

articles.title: Step 7: lui, leur in negatives, questions and the passé composé

blocks.en: *Lui* and *leur* follow the same places as *le, la, les*: *ne* before the pronoun, the pronoun before the auxiliary. One big difference: in the passé composé there is **no agreement**, because *lui* and *leur* are not COD.

articles.title: Step 8: le or lui? Mixing COD and COI

blocks.en: Now mix the two. Ask one question: **does the verb take *à* before the person?** Yes → *lui / leur*. No → *le / la / les*. *Je le vois* (I see him), but *Je lui parle* (I talk to him).

blocks.en: Many verbs take both: *donner* **quelque chose** (COD) **à quelqu'un** (COI). Each one has its own pronoun: *Je donne le livre à Paul → Je le donne à Paul* or *Je lui donne le livre*. Both at once is step 14.

articles.title: Step 9: me, te, nous, vous (and se)

blocks.en: For *me, you, us, you* French uses **one form for both COD and COI**: *me, te, nous, vous*. So you don't have to check the preposition, only the place. *Me* and *te* become **m'**, **t'** before a vowel.

items.fr: Il [[me]] voit.

items.fr: Il [[me]] parle.

items.en: I'll call you.
items.fr: Je [[t']]appelle.

items.en: She writes to us.
items.fr: Elle [[nous]] écrit.

blocks.en: When *me, te, nous, vous* are a **COD**, the participle agrees with the person they stand for: Marie says *Il m'a vue*. *Ils nous ont invités.* When they are a **COI** (*parler à, téléphoner à*), no agreement: *Elle nous a parlé.*
*Se (s')* is for the subject doing something to itself: *il se lave, elle s'appelle*. It sits in the same place as the other pronouns: *Il ne se lève pas. Elle va se coucher. Elle s'est levée.*

blocks.en: *Y* replaces **à + a thing or an idea** (*penser à l'examen*) and **a place** introduced by *à, en, dans, sur, chez* (*aller à Paris, être dans la chambre*). It goes in the usual spot: before the conjugated verb, or before the infinitive.

articles.title: Step 11: en for quantities and de + thing

blocks.en: *En* replaces **de + a thing** (*parler de, avoir besoin de*) and any noun with a **partitive or a quantity**: *du, de la, des, un, une, beaucoup de, trois...* The number or quantity word **stays at the end**: *J'en ai trois.*

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: *En* goes before the verb, the number or quantity word stays after it: *J'ai deux sœurs → J'en ai deux. Il a beaucoup d'amis → Il en a beaucoup. J'ai un chien → J'en ai un.* In the negative the number goes away: *Je n'en ai pas.*

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

*De* + a person is not *en*: *Je parle de Paul → Je parle de lui* (step 12).

articles.title: Step 12: people after a preposition: à lui, de lui, avec eux
articles.fr: les pronoms toniques après une préposition

blocks.en: When a **person** comes after a preposition and there is no object pronoun for that case, keep the preposition and use a **stressed pronoun**: *moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles*. *Je parle de Paul → Je parle de lui.*
*Parler de, avoir peur de, s'occuper de, être fier de, se souvenir de, avoir besoin de*: a thing becomes *en*, a person becomes *de* + stressed pronoun.

items.en: I'm talking about the film.
items.fr: J'[[en]] parle.

items.en: I'm talking about Paul.
items.fr: Je parle [[de lui]].

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: A few verbs keep *à* + stressed pronoun for people instead of *lui / leur*: *penser à, faire attention à, s'intéresser à, tenir à*, and *être à* (to belong to). *Je pense à Marie → Je pense à elle. Ce livre est à moi.*

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: After *avec, pour, chez, sans, devant, derrière, à côté de* a person is always a stressed pronoun: *Je vais chez lui. C'est pour toi. Il est assis à côté d'elle.*

item.task_en: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun

blocks.en: Stressed pronouns also stand alone and after *c'est*: *Qui veut du gâteau ? Moi ! C'est lui. Moi, je préfère le thé.*

items.fr: Ton grand-père ? Je pense souvent à lui.
items.en: Your grandfather? I often think about him.

items.fr: Mes petites sœurs ? Je m'occupe d'elles le mercredi.
items.en: My little sisters? I look after them on Wednesdays.

items.fr: Ce soir, on dîne chez eux.
items.en: Tonight we're having dinner at their place.

items.fr: Tu viens avec nous ?
items.en: Are you coming with us?

items.fr: Ce sac est à toi ?
items.en: Is this bag yours?

blocks.en: With two pronouns the order is fixed: **me / te / se / nous / vous → le / la / les → lui / leur → y → en**. Both go where one pronoun would go. *Il me le donne. Je le lui donne. Il m'en donne.*

sections.title: The pairs you will use most

blocks.en: *Lui* and *leur* never go together with *me, te, nous, vous*. In that case use *à* + stressed pronoun for the person: *Je te présente à lui.*

articles.title: Step 15: commands: Donne-le-moi ! Ne le donne pas !

blocks.en: In an **affirmative** command the pronoun goes **after** the verb, joined with a hyphen, and *me, te* become **moi, toi**: *Regarde-moi ! Prends-le !* In a **negative** command everything goes back to normal: *Ne me regarde pas ! Ne le prends pas !*

items.en: Take it!
items.fr: Prends-[[le]] !

items.en: Don't take it!
items.fr: Ne [[le]] prends pas !

blocks.en: The *tu* form of *-er* verbs (and *aller*) loses its *-s* in commands, but gets it back before *y* and *en* for the sound: *Va ! → Vas-y !*, *Mange ! → Manges-en !*

item.task_en: Turn it into a command and replace the underlined words

blocks.en: In an affirmative command the COD comes first, the other one second: *Donne-le-moi ! Donne-les-leur ! Montre-la-nous !* With *en*: *moi + en → m'en*: *Donne-m'en !*

item.task_en: Turn it into a command and replace the underlined words

blocks.en: *Ne* before the pronouns, *pas* after the verb, normal order, and *moi, toi* go back to *me, te*: *Aide-moi ! → Ne m'aide pas !* *Donne-le-moi ! → Ne me le donne pas !*
